label: M2.4-B protocol amendment 1: blinding (reveal timing) - made before any human session
flaw: the original launcher revealed the policy after each session once its ratings were saved; every block holds exactly one A and one B, so revealing one session makes its partner known, and per-session feedback lets the player learn behavioural signatures for later sessions
new_reveal_rule: no identity is shown after individual sessions; the player sees only "Response saved. Policy identity remains blinded."; after 30 / 30 rated sessions `reveal` locks the ratings (sha256 per session file + read-only), verifies the key against the manifest and every commitment, then decodes the assignments; analysis refuses to run before the lock and reveal
additional_blinding_changes: all stdout / stderr of the game process (Python and C level, including warnings and error text) goes to a private per-attempt log
session files store only the commitment, never the policy
the per-session strikes / hits summary is no longer printed
error details are never printed; only a neutral "ended early or error" message
unchanged: 15 paired blocks, same world seed per block

visible_channel_audit.window_title: "MaleCNS fly-swatter" for both policies (recorded by the smoke test)
visible_channel_audit.hud: gameplay HUD identical for both policies (time, strikes, hits, misses, escapes, rates, REC dot, key hints); neural HUD forced off by a read-only property; an injected H key leaves it off
visible_channel_audit.startup_messages: splash texts "Loading MaleCNS connectome ..." / "Compiling simulation kernels ..." identical
visible_channel_audit.terminal_stdout_stderr: game output redirected to a private log; launcher text neutral; scanned for identity tokens
visible_channel_audit.checkpoint_filename_path: never printed (loaded inside the private-output block)
visible_channel_audit.policy_class_name: never printed in the play flow (only the developer `smoke` mode prints it, on a synthetic seed)
visible_channel_audit.recorder_names: directory = UTC timestamp + random uuid; fixed file names; the recorder manifest (policy_class) is a private artifact under artifacts/m2_4_b/
visible_channel_audit.inherent_channel: the fly behaviour itself (the thing being evaluated)

smoke_test.sandbox: temporary directory, synthetic key, synthetic scripted inputs; never the real manifest; no real human response created
smoke_test.note: sandbox block 1 holds one A and one B session, so both policy paths were scanned
